text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Manzoor Wattoo resigned as Punjab province chief minister hours after 127 deputies withdrew a no-confidence motion against him and 98 deputies relinquished their assembly seats.

- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said his government would try to come up to the expectations of the people by taking to task the "umpteen corrupt" among the politicians, bureaucrats and the public.
- Federal minister for petroleum and natural resources Javed Jabbar said the government was reviewing gas prices and would rationalise them.
- The caretaker government will announce a series of economic reforms in December, said Finance and Economic Affairs Advisor Shahid Javed Burki.
- Commerce Minister Mohammad Zubair Khan said the rupee will not be devalued any further and said the government will announce a relief package for the textile industry.
- The prime minister's adviser on economic affairs Shahid Javed Burki said economic reforms introduced by the caretaker government will remain effective even after the February 3 polls.
- Despite heavy loan repayments in December, Pakistan would still be able to have liquid forex reserves in excess of $1.0 billion by end-1996, a government official said.
- Multinational vegetable ghee manufacturers increased their prices by 5.50 rupees per kg while local manufacturers have raised their prices between 2.0 to 3.0 rupees per kg.
- Drug enforcement agencies seized 12 tonnes of hashish from a container in Karachi port which had been brought from Faisalabad for shipment to Netherlands.
